newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-FRANCE BOUNCE BACK WITH THREE-GOAL BLAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FRANCE BOUNCE BACK WITH THREE-GOAL BLAST.

text.p: France, trounced 3-0 by Brazil in their opening match, bounced back by beating South Korea 4-2 in the world youth soccer championship on Thursday.

Three goals in the first 11 minutes fired the French to victory in the group C match, Thierry Henry scoring after two and 11 minutes and Monaco team mate David Trezeguet striking in the third and 53rd.
"We set our team to play that way," said coach Gerard Houllier. "We knew we would create chances and we started in the best way we could because we led after the first two attacks."
South Korean coach Park Lee Chung said: "Our chances of qualifying for the second round are scarce now but we will do our best to overcome Brazil."
Trailing 4-0, the South Koreans then started to apply pressure and pulled two goals back through Park Jin-sup, the first after 55 minutes.
Park was pulled down by Mikael Silvestre in the penalty box in the 69th minute. Jamaican referee Peter Prendergast pointed to the spot and Park tapped home his second goal.
Brazil beat South Africa 2-0 to retain the top spot in group C.
Hosts Malaysia, meanwhile, virtually ended their campaign by losing 3-0 to Uruguay in group A.
